Thanks for the invite. Quick heads up: our security team says external calendar invites that try to set organizer=external are being stripped by our tenant (they require organizer to be internal to our domain). When I click the Meet join button in the invite I get a 403 and the message says "Organizer not recognized by tenant." IT says they can whitelist links but only if we can send a standard Zoom URL in the body of the email instead of relying solely on the calendar join button.

We still want the demo — is there any chance you can either (A) send a plain Zoom link and copy it into the email body, or (B) have someone from your side create the calendar invite from an IST or admin account? Also, could we shift the demo window by 30 minutes — our VP has a sliding meeting. Proposed times: 10:30–11:00 PT or 11:00–11:30 PT tomorrow.

Appreciate it,
Samira

On it — thanks Samira for the detail.

Aditya, quick background: we've seen this tenant policy before (organizer rewrite). Two practical fixes we normally use:
- We email a plain Zoom link in the body and follow up with a calendar invite that marks our Redwood account as organizer (works for most SSO policies).
- Or we create the invite from a customer-facing support alias (events@redwood.com) so the organizer domain isn't rewritten.

Given this is a VP-level demo and they asked for a time shift, I recommend: send the Zoom backup link in the next email, and I'll recreate the calendar event from events@redwood.com and invite Samira & Tom. Laura — can you confirm events@redwood.com has the latest deck attached (redwood-demo-deck-v3.pdf) and the mutual action plan? I can also do a canary invite if you want to test the join button quickly.

Ben
